subject.title: feat(gateway): add context engine control API

question: Should OpenClaw expose context-engine capabilities, status, doctor, and rotate through a core Gateway/plugin control API after the session-targeting bug is fixed?
rationale: The session canonicalization defect is mechanical, but the permanent public HTTP methods, operator/admin scopes, and optional ContextEngine plugin hooks create a new compatibility-sensitive control contract that needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve after session fix
options.body: Keep the proposed status/doctor/rotate API direction, but require canonical session targeting, focused regression tests, scope review, and a clean merge state before landing.

options.title: Narrow to read-only control
options.body: Land only capabilities/status/doctor first and defer rotate until maintainers are ready to own an admin maintenance action.

options.title: Defer core control API
options.body: Pause or close the PR and keep context-engine maintenance control private/plugin-owned until a broader Gateway control contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve after session fix
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed status/doctor/rotate API direction, but require canonical session targeting, focused regression tests, scope review, and a clean merge state before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main Gateway/session helper history and the relevant CODEOWNERS-adjacent policy surface point most strongly to steipete for the API/session-boundary decision.
